### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via studio.access (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via studio.access (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via studio.access (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via studio.access (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1830d2ac735bc3345997e34c829fc73d5c58cb26` — the merge of head `0471b08e86fa876c4d45deeaf3e2a76a1993811c` into base `41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1830d2ac735bc3345997e34c829fc73d5c58cb26 && git checkout 1830d2ac735bc3345997e34c829fc73d5c58cb26
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e 0471b08e86fa876c4d45deeaf3e2a76a1993811c && git checkout -B drift-repro 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e && git merge --no-ff 0471b08e86fa876c4d45deeaf3e2a76a1993811c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 41babf7e649648e7d4b6fd6c5f0d3e8d6d7b406e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4320d105bfe447d10063811668035eff34ced4a8`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #37565 (body, claim, both claim amendments, triage, os-dev-report), PR #37602 (body, file list, net diff against `origin/main`), and the check-runs on this head. Every completed gate on the head is `success` or an opt-in `skipped`; one duplicate `Check Changeset` run was still `in_progress` when read, beside a completed `success` for the same name.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: nothing the server accepts or refuses changes. No spec, schema, route handler or metadata door is in the diff. The changes are client routing, one Setup navigation contribution (data), one registered component page, and labels.

Public-surface changes, each judged:

- `@objectstack/platform-objects`: `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` gains `nav_access_directory` in `group_access_control` (priority 100, `componentRef: 'security:access-directory'`, `requiredPermissions: ['studio.access']`). Plus one label in each of the 11 locale packs, with a source hash in each of the 10 non-English hash files. **Right.** This is data inside an existing export, and no export shape changes.
- `@object-ui/app-shell`: new `ACCESS_DIRECTORY_PATH` re-export from `index.ts`, plus new `views/setup/accessDirectory*.ts` and `AccessDirectoryPage.tsx`, and a new registered component ref. **Right.** The package is `"private": true`, so nothing is published from it and the re-export widens no published surface.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` Studio menu: the `environment` menu kind is removed from `StudioMenuEntryKind`, from the label map and from both icon maps. The `~org`/`~all` menus' catalog rows now open `accessDirectoryPath(type)`. **Right,** as claimed. The type is internal to a private package.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` fallback: `studioEntryFallbackPath` and `newPackageDoorPath` move from `/studio/~all/metadata` to `studioOrgScopePath()`. **Right,** and declared as temporary in the PR body and the changeset.
- Console `/studio/~all/*` now goes to `ACCESS_DIRECTORY_PATH` with `replace`. **Right.**
- `@object-ui/i18n` studio namespace: `engine.setup.accessDirectory.notAllowed` is added in `en` and `zh`. `engine.studio.notFound.allMetadata` keeps its key and changes its text to "Open organization flows" / 「组织流程」. **Right.**

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — security. In one permission state, the access gate of the new Setup page (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/AccessDirectoryPage.tsx`) is not at parity with the Studio entry gate it replaces. This breaches the card's own acceptance line: "opening it from Setup must not widen who sees it". The details are left out of this record on purpose and were given to the dispatching seat. The fix is small and local to that file and its test.
- S1 (should-fix) — Some re-pointed one-hop pins were weakened, which the card rules out ("re-pointed, not weakened"). In `ui/apps/console/src/__tests__/AppContent.systemHubRoutes.test.tsx` (both tables) and in the new `TO_SETUP_DIRECTORY` block of `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.setupMetadataStudio-28578.test.tsx`, the earlier `expect(chain).toEqual([from, to])` became `chain[0]` / `chain[1]` checks. A second hop after the landing now passes under a title that still says "in ONE hop". The fix is to restore the full-chain equality (as `AppContent.legacyRedirects`, `noAppComponentRoutes` and `pseudoRouteSegments` do). If the chain grows after landing for a reason that is not a hop, such as the list page's own `replace`, say so in the test.
- S2 (should-fix) — On `~org` (and on `~all` item pages), the catalog rows of the package-less menu now link to a Setup page. That page needs `setup.access` as well as `studio.access`. A Studio principal without `setup.access` (the repo's own `STUDIO_ONLY` fixture shape) is shown rows that lead to a refusal. Before this PR, the same rows opened in Studio. Gate those rows on Setup access, or record the dead end as accepted.
- N1 (nit) — `ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts`: the comment above `engine.studio.notFound.allMetadata` still says the way out is "the 'All metadata' area across packages". The value it describes now says "Open organization flows".
- N2 (nit) — `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` and `permission-sets.mdx` say "the old Studio and Setup catalog addresses redirect there". That holds only for the `?scope=environment` lists. A bare `/apps/setup/metadata/permission` (no scope) still lands on Studio's cross-package list, as before.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/37565-access-directory-in-setup.md` covers `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/console`, all at `patch`. It carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR body carries the same two lines.

- Level: **right.** AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3) says the level follows the metadata-protocol kind, and `none` takes `patch`. Nothing an author can write changes: a navigation contribution entry and labels are not authorable keys.
- Clause-②: **`no` is right.** No contract accept/reject behaviour changes on the server. The only new export (`ACCESS_DIRECTORY_PATH`) is in `@object-ui/app-shell`, which is `"private": true`, so it is not a public-surface widening. In `@objectstack/platform-objects` (published), only data inside the existing `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` export changes.
- Every package the diff moves is named in the changeset. The changeset on the private `app-shell` is harmless.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: the report's `open_questions` is `[]`. `security_findings` reads "none", and M1 above contradicts it. The one `out_of_scope_findings` entry is answered: the Setup page reuses the heading "All Metadata Types". It is noted on the PR and not filed. That is acceptable as a follow-up and not a blocker.
- The card's open question (#37424 comment 7188504633 (a)) is answered in the PR body: the package's 全部类型 directory still lists `datasource` and its tile still opens Setup → Datasources. The new Setup directory lists only the four environment types. **Accepted.**
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): there is no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The page mounts the existing metadata-admin pages and reads nothing new. **Clear.**

Security-touching: yes — the PR moves a capability-gated surface (the environment catalog of positions, permission sets, capabilities and sharing rules) and re-implements its `studio.access` gate in a new place, a Setup nav entry and a Setup page. See M1.

Seat questions:

1. **Who can reach it, before and after.** Before, the directory sat behind Studio's `RequireStudioAccess` (`studio.access` only). After, it sits behind the Setup app (`setup.access`), the nav entry's `requiredPermissions: ['studio.access']`, and the page's own `studio.access` check. Items, create and history still open in Studio behind the unchanged Studio gate. With a reported capability set, the page is strictly at or above the old rule. Holders of `studio.access` alone lose it, which is a narrowing the claim accepted. The Studio `~all` redirects run inside the Studio gate. The Setup legacy aliases (`/apps/…/system/permissions`, `/apps/setup/metadata`) now reach the page without passing the Studio gate, so the page's own gate decides, and M1 applies there. The Studio palette entry is gone (`StudioPaletteGroups.tsx`). Separately, the Setup nav entry's visibility goes through the shared nav `checkPerm`, whose object-read fallback is unchanged by this PR and is not reviewed here.
2. **Old addresses.** Every previous address still lands, and none is broken:
   - `/studio/~all`, `/studio/~all/…`, `/studio/~all/metadata` and the four types' `?scope=environment` lists land on the Setup page.
   - The legacy Setup catalog URLs and aliases land on the Setup page.
   - Items and cross-package lists of other types stay in Studio.

   Every redirect added is `Navigate … replace`: in `StudioRoute.tsx`, in `StudioMetadataArea.tsx` (the leg redirect is composed through `studioAddressAfterSetupMove`, so it stays one hop), and in `AccessDirectoryPage.tsx`. The zero-app alias pin in `AppContent.noAppComponentRoutes` pins something real. It asserts the full chain `[from, SETUP_DIRECTORY]`, which turns red if `studioAddressAfterSetupMove` is an identity. It also pins the destination's no-apps empty state, which every Setup page renders on a zero-app deployment. That is a real behaviour change (the alias used to open Studio's area there), and it follows from the accepted `setup.access` narrowing. Two other one-hop pins were loosened (S1).
3. **`Clause-②: no` at patch.** Right; see ②. `@object-ui/app-shell` is `"private": true` and not published, so the new re-export is not a widening.
4. **i18n.**
   - `platform-objects`: all 11 packs carry `nav_access_directory`, and all 10 hash files carry `apps.setup.navigation.nav_access_directory.label` with one shared English-source hash. They move together, and the i18n and stale-fill gates are green on the head.
   - Studio namespace: `en` and `zh` (the only two packs) are both updated.
   - Literals: the only new literals outside the packs are the component registration `label` and the `lazyPage` debug name, which is the sanctioned registry form used by the neighbouring registrations.
   - N1 is a stale comment, not a literal.
5. **Claim amendments.** Nothing lands outside the claim and its two amendments:
   - `index.ts`: one re-export.
   - `StudioEntryRedirect.tsx`: comment only (verified).
   - Docs: the four sentences/rows in `authorization.mdx`, `permission-sets.mdx` and `administrator-guide.mdx` (×2).
   - `StudioPaletteGroups.tsx`: the import and icon key only.

   The other touched files are all in the claimed file surface: the `StudioDesignSurface.*` tests are re-pointed tests and do not touch the fenced `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`; `accessDirectoryRef.ts` is a new file under `views/setup/`; the `notFound.allMetadata` text follows the claimed fallback change.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-x4tuqk`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

Use the same predicate as `RequireStudioAccess`, and pin parity with a test for every permission answer the Studio gate's own tests cover. The seat gave the details to the area directly.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2918cc2e38843878b43bfe909a5fb2d3e6b32481`
Local-runs: none

Delta review against the prior record on `4320d105` (FAIL), answering the seat's REWORK 7198240498.

Inputs read:
- the delta `pr-37602-a..pr-37602-b` (3 commits: `e0b4de63`, `c1dbc8fc`, `2918cc2e`; 21 files);
- the net diff against `origin/main` (63 files);
- the PR body at this head;
- the area's delta note (the latest PR comment);
- the check-runs on `2918cc2e`: 63 success, 11 skipped (opt-in or schedule lanes), none failed or pending.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: still unchanged. No server, spec or metadata-door code is in the delta.

Public-surface changes in the delta, each judged:

- `@object-ui/app-shell` adds `holdsSetupAccess` and `SETUP_ACCESS_CAPABILITY` (`views/setup/accessDirectoryRef.ts`), re-exported from `index.ts` on the line the amendment already approved. It also adds `holdsAccessDirectoryCapability` (`views/setup/accessDirectory.ts`). **Right.** The package is `"private": true`, and the console consumes the new export (`StudioRoute.tsx`).
- `buildStudioMenu` takes an optional `setupDirectory` that defaults to `false`. **Right.** Without it, package-less catalog rows keep the Studio environment-scope link, so the default is the safe one.
- The console's bare `/studio/~all/*` route is now `StudioAllLegAddress`: Setup's page for a `setup.access` holder, else `/studio/~all/metadata`. Both branches use `replace`. **Right.**
- In `StudioMetadataArea`, both the leg redirect and `studioAllLegSetupRedirect` are now gated on `holdsSetupAccess(useStudioEntryPermissions())`. **Right.**

Prior findings:

- M1 — **closed.** `AccessDirectoryPage` now decides with `holdsAccessDirectoryCapability(systemPermissions)`. That is `Array.isArray(...) && includes('studio.access')`, the same reading as the console's `holdsStudioAccess`. `AccessDirectoryPage.test.tsx` and `accessDirectory.test.ts` pin parity on each policy case the Studio gate names, with a control.
- S1 — **closed.** The full-chain `toEqual([from, to])` assertion is restored in both `AppContent.systemHubRoutes` tables and in the `TO_SETUP_DIRECTORY` block of `AppContent.setupMetadataStudio-28578`.
- S2 — **closed for the Studio side.** Package-less catalog rows open Setup only for a `setup.access` holder. Otherwise they keep `/studio/~all/metadata/TYPE?scope=environment`, and the leg still serves that list for them because both `~all` redirects are gated the same way. `holdsSetupAccess` refuses a set that was never reported, as `studioEntryPermissions.ts` already does. Both branches are tested in `studioMenuModel`, `StudioMenu`, `StudioMetadataArea.routes-28561` and the console `StudioRoute.metadataArea-28561`. One remainder is graded as S3.
- N1 — **closed.** The `en.ts` comment now names the organization's flows.
- N2 — **closed.** Both doc sentences now say that only the `?scope=environment` lists redirect, and only for a user who can open Setup.

New:

- S3 (should-fix) — The changeset and the PR body now say that a user who cannot open Setup "keeps these addresses in Studio". In the changeset, "these" includes "the old Setup metadata URLs that led there".
